evidence.note: Agent inspects test suites (c-testsuite, wacc) and states intent to 'build incrementally' and later run tests, but establishes no structured pass/fail tracking — only a vague plan.
A mismatched heredoc delimiter traps the shell at the PS2 prompt; from here the agent's monitoring is exclusively about shell state, never about test/feature progress.
Hundreds of steps repeating the same stuck-heredoc analysis; no test was ever executed, so no pass count, no done-vs-remaining ledger, and no regression watch ever existed.
Final steps still fighting the heredoc and re-checking whether the shell works; the compiler was never built and run_tests.sh never ran, so aggregate pass counts were never observed.

reasoning: The agent never built the compiler nor ran a single test, so it never obtained any pass count, never maintained a done-vs-remaining view, and never had the opportunity to detect regressions — placing it at the very bottom of the scale. It is above a pure 0 only because early on it enumerated the suites and voiced intent to track progress against tests, a faint gesture toward monitoring; but no structured tracking of 'what works vs. remains' ever materialized, matching level 1.
